coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Radiance

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint(s), not a hand trace or plan estimate. The underlying Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across many individually owned per-unit lots (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson), so no single blklot represents the whole building and it cannot be joined via status.csv the way a single-owner parcel can. Using the real building footprint from OSM instead of a fabricated or arbitrarily chosen 'representative' unit lot, the same real-geometry-without-a-single-parcel pattern already used for several Pier 70 buildings (DataSF Building Footprints) and for Mission Bay's own real park polygons.
notes.digitized_from: OpenStreetMap (way 1258086102, name=Radiance at Mission Bay, 325 China Basin St)

milestones.text: Radiance (325 China Basin St) offering its first homes as of a March 22, 2009 SFGate/Chronicle article ('Radiance offers first homes in Mission Bay'); Bosa's project page calls it the first major condominium development in the United States after the 2008 market downturn

changes.text: The map notes said Radiance is 9 stories per two realtor sources; of the readable sources, SFGate describes a nine-story and a six-story building and OSM has 8 levels, so the notes were rewritten. The 'first homes' milestone moved from September 2008 to March 2009, the date of the SFGate article that reports it, and the December 2006 groundbreaking milestone was removed because no readable source dates it. The OSM tag citation was corrected to name=.
changes.source: SFGate, 2009-03-22 (https://www.sfgate.com/realestate/article/Radiance-offers-first-homes-in-Mission-Bay-3247162.php); OpenStreetMap way 1258086102 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1258086102); Bosa Development, Radiance and Madrone, Mission Bay (https://bosadevelopment.com/project/radiance-madrone-mission-bay/)

record.notes: Story count: SFGate (March 22, 2009) describes Radiance Phase One as a nine-story building and a six-story building; the OSM way has building:levels 8. Bosa's page attributes the two connected 16-storey towers to Madrone, not Radiance.
